effects: Pulls exactly `assets` WETH from the signer into the vault (safeTransferFrom in enter).
Mints roxWETH shares to `onBehalf`. The number is previewDeposit(assets), worked out from the vault's stored totals. The calldata has no minimum for it.
Before this, accrueInterest mints fee shares to the fee recipients, which lowers the share price. The vault then sends the WETH to its liquidity adapter. Neither moves the signer's tokens.
formats.shown: Deposit 0.001 WETH for <onBehalf>, with the share ticker roxWETH as a constant field and onBehalf labelled 'Send shares to'.

findings.title: deposit: the number of roxWETH shares received is not shown, and no minimum is enforced.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit: `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);` comes from storage, and no minShares parameter exists. Case 0: signer receives 999999984000000 roxWETH, an amount the screen never states.
findings.fix: Nothing in calldata can bind it. A router with a slippage parameter would be needed.

findings.title: deposit: the 'Share ticker' constant field adds a line with no amount and repeats what the token already implies.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit field {label:'Share ticker', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker'} renders 'roxWETH' on its own.
findings.fix: Fold it into the label instead, e.g. 'Send roxWETH shares to'.

cases.notes: The 0.001 WETH leaving is shown right. The roxWETH shares going to the signer have the right asset and recipient, but the amount (999999984000000) cannot be shown from calldata.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns previewWithdraw(assets) roxWETH shares from `onBehalf`. The number is worked out from storage, and no maximum is set.
If the signer is not `onBehalf`, it spends that many shares of onBehalf's allowance to the signer.
Sends exactly `assets` WETH from the vault to `receiver`. The vault may first pull liquidity back from its adapter.
formats.shown: Withdraw 850 WETH to <receiver>, with Owner = onBehalf shown as a field.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of roxWETH shares burned from the owner is not shown, and no maximum is enforced.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw: `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);` then `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)`. Case 2: 844756059076460699199 roxWETH leaves the signer, and the screen shows no share amount.
findings.fix: Not in calldata. A wording such as 'Burns roxWETH shares from Owner' in the Owner label would at least name the asset.

findings.title: withdraw: the 'Owner' label does not say that this account's roxWETH shares are burned.
findings.evidence: descriptor withdraw field onBehalf label 'Owner'. Code: `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)` and the allowance spend `allowance[onBehalf][msg.sender] = _allowance - shares`.

cases.notes: The 850 WETH arriving at the signer is shown right. The reader guessed that shares were burned, but the roxWETH asset and amount are not on screen.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns exactly `shares` roxWETH from `onBehalf`. If the signer is not onBehalf, it spends that much of onBehalf's allowance to the signer.
Sends previewRedeem(shares) WETH to `receiver`. The amount is worked out from storage, and no minimum is set.
formats.shown: Redeem 30.41 roxWETH to <receiver>, with Owner = onBehalf. The asset paid out is never named.

findings.title: redeem: the screen never names WETH as the asset the receiver gets.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit: `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);`. The descriptor redeem fields only list shares, receiver and onBehalf. Case 3: signer receives 30636524139142703956 WETH. Reader: 'Which token I get back is not shown (WETH is a guess)'.
findings.fix: Add a constant field {label:'Receive asset', value:'$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker'} as mint does, and say 'Redeem {shares} for WETH to {receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem: the WETH amount received has no minimum, so the amount cannot be bound on screen.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem: `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);` comes from storage. No minAssets parameter exists.

cases.notes: The 30.41 roxWETH burned is shown right. The WETH received is not named and its amount is not shown, so the reader only guessed the asset.

effects: Pulls previewMint(shares) WETH from the signer. The amount is worked out from storage, and no maximum is set.
formats.shown: Mint <shares> roxWETH for <onBehalf>, with a constant 'Deposit asset: WETH' and no WETH amount.

findings.title: mint: the WETH amount taken from the signer is not shown, and no maximum is enforced.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint: `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares);` then `safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)`. Case 1: 1000000000 WETH leaves the signer, and the screen shows only 'WETH'.
findings.fix: Not in calldata. The cap is the signer's WETH allowance to the vault.

findings.title: mint: the intent 'Mint' does not say that the signer's WETH is pulled to pay for the shares.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint intent 'Mint' and interpolatedIntent 'Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'. The code pulls WETH from msg.sender in enter().
findings.fix: Use the intent 'Deposit WETH to mint shares' and the sentence 'Pay WETH to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: The WETH leaving is named as an asset, but its amount (1000000000 wei) is not shown. The shares went to 0xdead, not the signer.
